title: 1 man dead after being shot during confrontation with home invader, Toronto police say
summary: A man has died after a shooting during an attempted home invasion early Wednesday in Toronto, police say. They said an unknown number of suspects 'forced their way' into a home and shot a resident…

blocks.text: Toronto

A man has died after a shooting during an attempted home invasion early Wednesday in Toronto, police say. They said an unknown number of suspects 'forced their way' into a home and shot a resident during a confrontation.
Officers say they'll 'spare no expense' to investigate attempted home invasion in South Hill neighbourhood
Man killed during attemped home invasion near Casa Loma: police
A man has died after a shooting during an attempted home invasion early Wednesday in midtown Toronto, police say.
Emergency crews responded to reports of a shooting at a residence near Poplar Plains Road and St. Clair Avenue W. around 2:30 a.m., Det. Sgt. Alan Bartlett said at a news conference.
He said an unknown number of suspects "forced their way" into the home and soon after confronted a resident. One person was shot during that interaction, he said.
Paramedics said a man was taken to hospital in critical condition. He was later pronounced dead in hospital, Bartlett said.

"I understand and recognize how deeply troubling this must be, not only to the residents of that community, but to the residents of the city of Toronto as a whole," he said, adding there is no evidence to suggest the family was targeted for any specific reason.
"We are pursuing all investigative leads and residents in the area, as always, expect an increased uniform and non-uniform police presence."
The victim is believed to be the son of the homeowner, 53 Division Staff Sgt. Shain Griffin told CBC News.

Toronto police said there will be a heavy police in a midtown Toronto neighbourhood as investigators look for evidence after a fatal shooting during an attempted home invasion on Nov. 25, 2026. (Paul Smith/CBC)

Police are still working to notify the victim's next of kin and will not be providing any other details at this time, Bartlett said. There were a total of four residents inside the home at the time, he said.
Bartlett said Toronto police Chief Myron Demkiw assured him that every resource available will be provided to investigators and "no expense will be spared."
He said police do not yet have details on the number of suspects, any descriptions or what vehicles may have been used.
He urged anyone with surveillance video or any witnesses who saw anything between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. to contact police.
'Far too many' home invasions in Toronto: city councillor
Coun. Josh Matlow told reporters outside the home Wednesday there have been "far too many" home invasions throughout the city and that it needs to be a top priority to address residents' concerns.

"There's a feeling amongst Torontonians that far too often people go to bed at night worrying about whether or not they'll wake up to somebody in their home," Matlow said, adding there's work to do in the community to support "very scared" residents.
He said he has offered Demkiw his "complete support" during the investigation. He urged people to not jump to conclusions until investigators share more answers.
MPP Stephanie Smyth, who joined Matlow, said police do what they can to investigate incidents, but that more needs to be done to address the fear residents feel.

Coun. Josh Matlow and MPP Stephanie Smyth spoke to reporters outside the scene of a fatal home invasion on Wednesday. They shared their condolences for the victim's loved ones and reassured residents they will do their best to address fears. (Paul Smith/CBC)
"They can talk about the stats all they want, but the bottom line is people are afraid. And the one place you should not feel afraid is in your own home," she said.

Matlow added that "it's shameful" to hear that many residents in the neighbourhood and nearby areas have hired private security to safeguard their homes. Smyth said there needs to be stronger deterrence for these crimes, such as harsher penalties.
"People have to do what they feel is the right choice to ensure the safety of their family," Bartlett said in regards to some people hiring private security.

When asked what tips he had for residents regarding a potential home invasion, he said people should call 911 immediately and that Toronto Police Service "provides the best that it can in terms of public safety services."
"Oftentimes we can't provide the why, we simply don't know. What my promise has been to the victims' family is that we'll do our very best to provide the who."
Incident follows Bridle Path home invasion last month

The incident comes nearly a month after a home invasion and shooting hospitalized a family of four adults in Toronto's Bridle Path neighbourhood. Police arrested one suspect in Ottawa last week and are looking for two others.

Toronto police have been investigating and patrolling to deter home invasions in parts of the city after seeing a rise in incidents earlier this year, Demkiw said in remarks to the Toronto Police Service Board back in July.

Here's where home invasions are happening in Toronto and what's being done to prevent them

blocks.text: He said the service launched this initiative in areas that saw the largest increase in home invasions, which includes 22, 32 and 53 Divisions. The 22 division covers neighbourhoods in central and southern Etobicoke, 32 operates in central and western North York, and 53 Division covers central and midtown Toronto.
"We continue to put our people and our resources where we see challenges, and where we hear concerns from our communities," Demkiw told the police board.

Home invasions hit a 10-year high in 2024, before dropping in 2025 and then rising again at the beginning of this year in Toronto, according to CBC News analysis of Toronto police data. Affluent areas with large detached houses and driveways were among the hardest hit.
